decision.title: Enhanced video editing: TSX-first timeline op layer (ripple engine + clip-ops module, one /_api/clip-edit dispatch route, hard-cut gate relaxation, TransitionSeries default container, AIPlaceholder primitive)
decision.rationale: feature-enhanced-video-editing execution (Phases 0-5). Structural decisions: (1) NEW MODULES apps/studio/ripple.ts (pure ripple engine: literal + additive-const-expression rewrites, const-aware double-shift guard, structured RippleError refusals) and apps/studio/clip-ops.ts (composed verbs: remove-rippled, series MOVE, positional insertClipAt, split, speed/trim-in/audio/detach/framing/grade, transition insert/edit/remove, resolve-placeholder) — kept OUTSIDE canvas-edit.ts so the import graph stays acyclic (ripple imports canvas-edit). (2) ONE dispatch route POST /_api/clip-edit with a verb field instead of per-verb routes — smaller DDR-054 main-origin surface, one canvas-origin-gate assertion, and it doubles as the agent door for /design:edit timeline vocabulary (manual UI and agents speak the identical API). (3) assertCompSemantics RELAXED: adjacent Sequences (hard cuts) are valid Remotion and exist in shipped canvases; the gate now refuses only leading/trailing/doubled Transitions — the old strict alternation refused every op on hard-cut comps. (4) assembleCompSource now emits a TransitionSeries storyline (Blueprint default-container rule: series membership = magnetic butting + seam transitions) and accepts empty clips[] as the greenfield New-video scaffold. (5) AIPlaceholder added to canvas-lib.tsx: prompt-carrying slate clip resolved in place via the DDR-164 generation spine; prompt always JSON.stringified (DDR-150 P1). (6) Timeline comments extended the existing comment store with a timeline anchor {clipStableId, frameOffset}|{frame} rather than a new store. (7) trimBefore is the canonical in-point spelling (startFrom read as legacy, retired on write). Rejected: EDL-as-live-document (round-trip lossiness, DDR-150 P1 at document scale) and adopting an external editor (per the plan debate).

decision.title: Shell text input never uses window.prompt — WKWebView no-op; promise-based shell modal (askText) is the house mechanism
decision.rationale: Dogfood finding (enhanced-video-editing desktop testing): Tauri WKWebView does not implement window.prompt() — it returns null synchronously, so every prompt-driven feature (AI placeholder insert, + Title, New video…, timeline comments) silently did nothing in the desktop app while working in Chromium. Decision: the shell owns ONE promise-based modal (askText(title, initial) → Promise<string|null>, state + .st-prompt dialog in app.jsx); panels receive it as a promptText prop rather than calling window.prompt. Rule for future shell/panel code: never call window.prompt/confirm for user text in the studio client — route through askText (or a richer dialog). Also recorded from the same session: tauri dev serves resources from a target/debug copy that a fast restart does not refresh — a stale client bundle in dev is fixed by copying apps/studio/dist into target/debug/apps/studio/dist (or a full cargo rebuild), worth knowing before chasing phantom UI bugs.

decision.title: kind="video" artboard is the video intent: storyline drop auto-injects a VideoComp in place (applyEnsureVideoComp); New Cut canvas is only the no-eligible-artboard fallback
decision.rationale: Dogfood finding (enhanced-video-editing): the Inspector lets a user set a DCArtboard kind to video, but nothing connected that to the timeline — a brief-board artboard marked kind=video still had no <VideoComp>, so timeline drops dead-ended (first as a refusal, then as a surprising auto-created New Cut canvas). Decision: applyEnsureVideoComp (clip-ops.ts) upgrades a kind="video" artboard IN PLACE on the first storyline insert — injects a unique const <Name> comp (AbsoluteFill root, the greenfield insert contract) + a <VideoComp> mounted as the artboard last child sized to the artboard, then retries the insert. applyInsertClipAt calls it automatically when the comp is missing and lane=storyline. The drop flow ORDER is: (1) in-place upgrade of an opted-in artboard, (2) only then the New Cut fallback canvas. An explicit artboardId that is NOT kind=video does not get auto-upgraded (opt-in stays with the user via the Inspector Kind picker). This also gives the Kind picker real semantics; the reverse conversion (video → digital, i.e. removing the VideoComp) remains an open follow-up. Also fixed structurally this session: tauri.conf beforeDevCommand switched to { script, wait: true } — the default no-wait raced the resource staging (rmSync + restage) against cargo build.rs, which is why warm dev restarts randomly panicked with ENOENT and served stale bundles.

decision.title: Debate: Timeline UX polish direction — orientation/hierarchy first, predictive drag feedback second, tokenised micro-motion last
decision.rationale: Divergent debate (reduce), 3 seats over the dogfood complaint (drag placeholders, micro-animations, scattered/uninformative layout). Converged direction: (1) ORIENTATION — storyline as the dominant inset trough with overlays recessed and audio distinct; V1/V2/A1 lane-identity chips in a left-aligned gutter; human clip names (never content-hash filenames); one shared frame; the dead space below the lanes becomes the labelled new-layer drop zone; playhead carries its own timecode chip. (2) PREDICTIVE FEEDBACK — dragged beat lifts (scale+shadow+grabbing), storyline glows as the vertical-move drop target, momentary accent snap-line whenever a drag latches (magnetism was invisible), trim/seam affordances visible at rest and promoted on hover. (3) MOTION — all transitions through DS --dur-*/--ease-* tokens, transform/opacity only, collapsed under prefers-reduced-motion. Seat votes: BUILDER polish-first 0.72, DESIGN-CRITIC polish-first 0.72, USER-ADVOCATE restructure-first 0.75 (its restructure = the same information layer; no seat argued animations-first).

decision.title: Timeline dogfood round 3: inline-editable text, z-order verb, C comment tool
decision.rationale: User steer 2026-07-30: (1) AI placeholder drops the modal — emitted as paired-tag {"prompt"} so the prompt is a stamped data-cd-editable leaf, double-click-editable in the artboard; Title overlay inner div gets pointerEvents:auto for the same reason. (2) New clip-edit verb layer-order {toIndex} — vertical z-order of standalone overlay clips; doc order = paint order, audio excluded; UI = V-chip drag + context menu. Overlay band renders top = topmost paint. (3) Comment tool C arms click-to-place on the timeline; anchor gains lane (V1/V2../A1) and pins render in-lane on the clip at frameOffset. (4) Loose bare media siblings (outside every Sequence) now render as read-only rows (previously invisible). (5) Decomposable storyline beats expand into layer sub-rows in band mode (restores the pre-band per-layer view for old hand-authored comps).

decision.title: Debug desktop builds never auto-update
decision.rationale: tauri dev dogfooding was broken by the silent auto-update loop: the dev app (running in-flight worktree changes) found the newer released version, downloaded it, and restarted itself INTO the installed release mid-test (observed 2026-07-30 with 0.49.2-dev vs released 0.50.0) — the tester unknowingly evaluated the wrong build, and repeated dev launches appeared to be mysteriously killed. Fix: updater.rs gates the silent paths (spawn_update_loop background loop + check_now focus check) on cfg!(debug_assertions) — a debug build logs "[maude] debug build — background auto-update disabled" and never self-replaces. The explicit Maude ▸ Check for Updates… menu path (check_now_interactive) stays functional in debug so the flow itself remains testable. Release builds are unchanged (DDR-126 auto-update posture).

decision.title: Timeline dogfood round 4: stacked projection for pure-JSX comps, anchored comment composer
decision.rationale: User steer 2026-07-30 (round 4): (1) Band/iMovie layout is for MEDIA cuts only — a purely digital comp (every sequence a hand-authored JSX scene, e.g. Maude Video Intro) keeps the stacked row-per-sequence projection with layer expansion; heuristic bandMode = storyline present AND any non-jsx sequence. (2) Timeline comments compose in a small popover ANCHORED at the click (artboard comment grammar) — the center-screen shell modal is gone from both the C tool and the context menu path. (3) AIPlaceholder slate drops the AI-kind chip (prompt text only). (4) Filmstrip extraction keeps the <video> attached to the document with explicit load() — WKWebView refuses to decode a detached element (the desktop no-filmstrips bug); failures now log to console. (5) tlci popover + chips restyled to the DS inspector-controls voice (mono uppercase micro-labels, hairline border-subtle, squared segments, accent-tint active).
